full_judgment:
Plaintiff-Petitioners laid a Suit being Title Suit No. 33 of 1989 in the First Court of learned Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge. Sunamganj for a decree of Partition in respect of 2.40-3/4 acres of property which has been described in schedule to plaint. Plaintiffs-petitioners rested their claim on the strength of a registered kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919. Record of Right had not been fully prepared in the name of plaintiffs-petitioners but the same had been recorded in the name of defendants-opposite parties. 

 I. Property of Lakshmipur and Singua Mouza were measured and there had been no identity of the land conveyed in the kabuliyat with schedule property. In coming to decision, learned Trial Judge took into account evidence of PW 5, Advocate Commissioner who made disclosure in his evidence that he did not mention in his report that he did not find any similarity in respect of plots of Kabuliyat and, also, he did not mention the quantity of land conveyed in kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919. 

 IV. Plaintiffs did not mention all lands noted in kabuliyat and deeds in schedule and plaintiff suit is barred by doctrine of hotchpot. In coming to said decision learned Trial Judge examined Kabuliyat and documents. 

 V. Plaintiffs in schedule had mentioned less land of the lands noted in kabuliyat and deed and no grounds had been assigned to that effect. 

 VIII. Plaintiffs in support of title on the basis of Kabuliyat did not produce any documentary evidence and plaintiff did not produce any evidence in support of case tabled by them that landlords accepted them as tenants on granting Rent Receipts. 

 30. Admittedly, suit is for decree of partition in respect of 2.40-3/4 acres of property and the basis of claim of plaintiffs-petitioners is a kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919. 

 31. Learned Trial Judge in dismissing the suit considered evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner who laid bare evidence that he on local investigation did not find the similarity with all the plots noted in kabuliyat and he, also, did not make any report. Advocate Commissioner PW 5, also, did not state the quantity of land transferred in the kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919. Learned Trial Judge found inconsistency and infirmity in respect of quantity of land converted by kabuliyat. Learned Trial Judge, also, took into account evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner who laid bare in evidence that he was not at all aware of land converted in the kabuliyat. Learned Trial Judge taking into account the evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner came to hold that land of Lakshmipur and Singua Mouza had been measured and there had been no identity of land conveyed in kabuliyat with the schedule land described in plaint and suit is barred by the defect of hotchpotch. Learned Appellate Judge concurred with findings reached by learned Trial Judge. 

 32. In order to attract the land of kabuliyat with the land described in schedule to plaint the identify of property was required to be relayed by a Survey-trained Advocate Commissioner and by relayment identity of the land noted in kabuliyat with schedule land could not be at all ascertained and established. Non-identity of land conveyed in kabuliyat with schedule land described in plaint is definitely a "formal defect" of fundamental nature and the suit must fail for this "formal and material defect." 

 38. Defects occurred could have been possibly remedied by way of an amendment in the suit and, in the event of allowing amendment, suit might relate back to initial stage of the suit, inasmuch as the defendant side got the right to lay additional written statement and would take other steps which would have definitely encumbered the suit. Moreover, by way of amendment "formal defects" of fundamental nature such as, identity of land conveyed in kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919 with the suit land could not be at all remedied. Even in the event of amendment, in the absence of identification of land conveyed in kabuliyat with suit land suit might fail for inherent defect. Amendment of plaint, thus, might not have been proper substitute and "formal defects" and all controversies can be solved if a fresh suit is instituted on curing all defects which is the spirit behind the provision engrafted in Order XXIII, rule 1 of the Code.
